column2: Israel lodges at Shittim and is profaned through sexual immorality with Moab's daughters. The reflexive English conveys their participation without changing the act.
Invitation, sacrificial eating and bowing to idols remain successive actions. Both idol references are retained.
Initiation into Baal of Peor's worship represents the selected cultic verb, followed by divine anger.
All leaders are taken and publicly exposed before the Lord in sunlight. The selected verb is not narrowed to a specific execution method absent here.
Moses addresses tribes, not judges, and commands each to kill his own initiated kinsman. Both distinctive selected details remain.
The selected man brings his brother to the Midianite woman before Moses and the weeping assembly. The roles are not reversed to match a familiar alternative.
Phinehas is identified through Eleazar and Aaron; he rises and takes a lance, with the action continuing into verse 8.

Propose kiln for the selected kaminos instead of chamber. A bounded lexical inquiry found LSJ's alcove gloss but also a scholarly critique tracing its uncertain basis and arguing from the ordinary kiln sense; see lexical-checks.json. The two victims, womb and cessation of plague remain.
column3: The cited papyri and specialist commentaries were not independently inspected; the architectural identification remains provisional.

column2: The toll is 24,000; it is not harmonized with a different number in another text.
The Lord's speech introduces the explanation and covenant.
Phinehas' genealogy repeats; his zeal shares God's zeal and halts wrath, preventing consumption of Israel.
A covenant of peace is expressly given to Phinehas.
The covenant extends priesthood to his seed because of zeal for God and atonement for Israel. Both stated grounds remain.
Zimri son of Salu is a Simeonite ancestral-house ruler. The selected name pair remains in provisional conventional English.
Cozbi daughter of Zur is identified with Ommoth and a Midianite ancestral house. Ommoth is retained rather than removed as unfamiliar.
column3: The name and appositional relationships require fuller name/syntax review.

column2: The selected longer introduction commands Moses to speak to Israel before the hostility instruction.
Hostility and striking the Midianites are both commanded. The historical command is retained without softening or modern application.
Deceit concerning Peor and Cozbi explains the hostility; her kinship and death on the plague day remain.
After the plague the Lord addresses Moses and Eleazar, establishing the changed priestly partner for the census.
The census includes the whole assembly's battle-ready men from twenty upward by ancestral houses.
Moses and Eleazar speak in Araboth of Moab beside Jordan opposite Jericho. The selected place form is retained.
The twenty-and-upward threshold repeats before the heading for Israel's descendants from Egypt. The abrupt transition remains.
Reuben is firstborn; Hanoch and Pallu lead his clan list. Greek personal and clan forms correspond without importing extra names.
Hezron and Carmi complete Reuben's four-clan list.
Reuben's selected total is 43,730, correctly retained in English.
Plural sons introduces Eliab alone, as in the selected source; no additional son is supplied.
Nemuel, Dathan and Abiram are named before the uprising explanation against Moses, Aaron and the Lord.
column3: The scope of the following these references across the three-name list remains a discourse question.

column2: Earth swallows the rebels and Korah; fire consumes 250 and they become a sign. The selected explicit Korah object remains.
Korah's sons explicitly do not die. The exception is not suppressed to harmonize the preceding account.
Simeon's list begins Nemuel, Jamin and Jachin, with the repeated clan heading retained.
Zerah and Shaul complete Simeon's list.
Simeon's census is 22,200, matching the selected Greek.
Judah's Er and Onan died in Canaan; the location and both names remain.
Shelon, Perez and Zerah are Judah's clan heads in the selected forms.
Perez's branches are Hezron and Iamun; Iamun is not silently changed to a familiar alternative name.
Judah's total is 76,500.
Issachar's first two clans are Tola and Puah.
Jashub and Shimron complete Issachar's four-clan list; the conventional equivalents remain provisional.
Issachar's total is 64,300.
Zebulun's selected names are Sered, Allon and Allel. The last two are not harmonized to alternative lists.
Zebulun's total is 60,500.
Gad follows Zebulun in this selected chapter, beginning Zephon, Haggi and Shuni.
Ozni and Addi continue Gad's list; Addi remains the selected distinctive name.
Arod and Ariel complete Gad's list. Ariel is not substituted with another traditional name.
Gad's total is 40,500.
Asher follows Gad, with Jamin, Ishvi and Beriah. The selected Jamin is retained.
Heber and Malchiel continue Asher's list, without an added genealogical clause between verses.
Asher's daughter is Sarah in the selected Greek form, retained provisionally rather than normalized to Serah.
Asher's total is 53,400.
Joseph's sons are Manasseh and Ephraim in that order, introducing their distinct counts.
Machir begets Gilead, and each has a named clan. The father-son relation remains explicit.
Gilead's list begins Ahiezer and Helek; Ahiezer follows the selected name rather than an alternate form.
Esriel and Shechem continue Gilead's clans.
Symaer and Hepher complete the list, retaining Symaer's distinctive selected form.
Zelophehad has daughters only: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah. All five and their order remain.
Manasseh's total is 52,700.
Ephraim's selected list names Shuthelah and Tanach only; no missing clan is supplied from another tradition.
Eden is Shuthelah's branch in the selected text, not replaced by a familiar alternate name.
Ephraim's total is 32,500, followed by the summary of Joseph's clans.
Benjamin's list begins Bela, Asyber and Iachiran, retaining selected forms provisionally.
Sophan continues Benjamin's list as the sole name in this unit.
Bela's sons Adar and Naaman each have a clan. Both the kinship statement and repeated clan names remain.
Benjamin's total is 45,600.
Dan's clan is Sami in the selected text; the repeated Dan/clan formula remains.
All Sami clans total 64,400, preserving the plural collective description despite one named ancestor.
Naphtali's list begins Asiel and Guni.
Jezer and Shillem complete Naphtali's clans, in the selected order.
Naphtali's total is 45,400.
The stated Israel total is 601,730; the twelve manually compared tribal figures sum to it. Arithmetic is recorded separately.
Divine speech introduces land distribution after the counts.
Land is allotted to these by the number of names, preserving the connection between registration and inheritance.
Larger and smaller groups receive proportionate inheritances according to their census. Both increase and decrease remain.
The land is divided by lots according to ancestral tribal names. Proportionality is not used to erase the stated lots.
Lots govern distribution between more and fewer; the repeated relationship remains.
The separate Levitical list names Gershon, Kohath and Merari with their clans.
Libni, Hebron, Korah and Mushi are listed, then Kohath begets Amram. No extra clan from another list is inserted.
The selected wording says Jochebed bore these to Levi in Egypt and then bore Aaron, Moses and Miriam to Amram. The difficult sequence is not corrected by conjecture.

column2: Nadab and Abihu die offering strange fire, with the selected Sinai-wilderness location retained.
Levitical males from one month total 23,000, separate from Israel's census because they receive no land allotment.
Moses and Eleazar's census setting repeats Araboth, Jordan and Jericho.
No man from Moses and Aaron's earlier Sinai census remains among this group, preparing the explicit exception next.
The wilderness death sentence is emphatic; Caleb and Joshua alone remain as the named exceptions.
